$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
believe about it. Same two buckets as TAIPANBOX/vouchryx, which is where
this shape was worked out, and the same reason for being here rather than
in estate-gates: the only thing that knows which binaries a repository
This one differs from vouchryx in a way worth stating, because it is what
a launcher trips over: it is configured by FLAGS and not by the
environment. Two variables are read and neither is how a deployment wires
it. So `checked.flags` carries what `checked.env` carries elsewhere, and
manifest_test.go proves it the same way, against the flag.String call

role.value: the FinOps console: cloud and AI spend, an agent crew that triages it, and a person who reviews what they wrote
role.why: a sentence about purpose is not a property of the source

enforces_nothing.why: it has no gateway, no interceptor and no refusal path, and `internal/enforce` is a separate binary this console never imports. Every budget_threshold it emits carries `enforced: false`, stamped by the translation rather than by the caller. Checkable only as an absence, and an absence today is not a promise about tomorrow, so it is declared and heraldyx's catalog rests on it.

the_event_file_name_is_the_integration.why: genaryx tails a directory and keys each source's read offset off the file stem, so a stream under any other name is a stream it never reads. Nothing in THIS repository can check a consumer's behaviour, and the flag accepts any path.

off_unless_asked.why: the whole stack integration is off when that flag is empty, which is the default. A deployment that forgets it gets a working console and an empty bus, and no error, because a console nobody wired to a stack is a legitimate way to run this.

passports_and_owner_are_a_pair.why: the console refuses to start with the first and not the second: a passport with no owner is not a valid document, and idryx enriches an identity with the owner who answers for it, so one that names nobody enriches nothing. A dependency BETWEEN two flags is not something a reader of flag.String call sites can see, which is why it is declared. Found by TAIPANBOX/stack-up on 2026-08-28, by starting it.

oidc_is_all_or_nothing.why: sign-in through an identity provider is off unless -oidc-issuer is set, and once it is set the console refuses to start without the other four: a provider with no role mapping could let nobody in, and there is no default role. The client secret has no flag on purpose, because a flag's value is visible in the process list. While it is set, /signup is closed and the console reaches that provider, the second of the two outbound doors invariant 64 names. A dependency between settings is not visible from flag.String call sites, so it is declared (invariants 74 and 75).

typryx_sends_only_the_template_fields.why: off when the flag and COSTCREW_TYPRYX_URL are empty, the default. Set, the console asks typryx's triage.anomaly_class template for a typed hint about each open anomaly after detection, sending only the fields that template names from a closed vocabulary that holds no team, owner, agent or person, and records which backend answered. Where those fields then go (nowhere, an operator's own model, or Jev hosted by TypeSafe AI) is typryx's TYPRYX_BACKEND, which nothing in this repository can see. The third of the outbound doors invariant 64 names (invariant 77).

role.value: pushes decided unit budgets to TokenFuse, plan and apply, fingerprint-bound

the_only_thing_here_that_changes_another.why: it makes an HTTP call that changes the number a gateway uses to decide whether to refuse a call. The console never invokes it; that separation is the reason `enforces_nothing` above is true, and it is a fact about which package imports which rather than one a manifest can prove.

role.value: writes the `agents` source idryx asks for, so this console's crew appears in the identity graph
the parity gate against the captured golden surface

scores an analyst's named cause against the known driver on the generated fixture (or, on imported data with no driver, against the posted/returned stamp), so a FinOps lead reads a percentage rather than a pile of deliverables

holds_no_caller_at_all.why: -live refuses unconditionally: with a mock engine because neither mock is ever selectable with it, and with a real one because this binary imports no HTTP client and reads no model-provider credential (checked by reading tools/bench's own source, not merely by this flag's default). A live run waits for a shared caller in internal/deliver, so that tools/run's TokenFuse gateway covers this binary's calls too; not built yet.

role.value: reconciles the generated estate's own planes (utilisation rows, SaaS seats, commitments) against the generated ledger, world.Generate(), for the last full month, and prints where they do not add up; it opens no store, reads no cloud account and makes no network call (its only imports are fmt, internal/money and internal/world). The AWS Data Exports and GCP billing export folder readers that make a real customer estate reach the crew are connectors in internal/connectors, which this tool does not use (costcrew#68)
runs the crew against the open board, live, against a real model provider

spends_real_money.why: it calls a paid provider with a key the operator supplies. Nothing in the source distinguishes a paid endpoint from a free one, and a manifest that claimed to know would be guessing about somebody else's billing.

the_gateway_has_one_door_per_wire.value: -gateway fronts the Anthropic wire and -gateway-openai fronts the OpenAI wire (openrouter); with either set, a call goes through the gateway that fronts its engine or is refused, never sent direct
the_gateway_has_one_door_per_wire.why: TokenFuse forwards ONE upstream wire shape per process (its TOKENFUSE_WIRE), so the two wires are two gateway processes and two URLs. Bedrock speaks neither, so with any gateway set a bedrock call is refused. Not checkable from outside this repository: the routing is deliver.Gateway.RouteFor in internal/deliver/call.go, and which TokenFuse process is behind each URL is the operator's setup, not something a manifest can see.

role.value: writes agent-events onto the shared bus from outside the console

bypasses_the_translation.why: it builds the envelope itself rather than going through internal/stack, so the two-row vocabulary table does not apply to it and its emitted type set is whatever a caller passes. A deployment feeding the bus from here rather than from the console is emitting types nothing registered.
